newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts to make break for 114-30,31.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts to make break for 114-30,31.

text.p: September gilt futures on LIFFE will have a run at 114-30,31 on Monday, helped by strong showings in Bunds and the U.S. market, technical analysts said.
"It's all following the U.S. from Friday," Norman Beauchamp, head of derivatives at Cooperative Bank in London, said.
"The key is whether or not we can get through 114-30. That's going to be the target. If it can't break through there then it will probably just move sideways," he said.
September gilts hit a contract high of 114-31 on May 9. They closed on Friday at 114-02 after slower than expected jobs growth in the U.S. lifted all debt markets.
"If we get through there (114-30,31) then you're off to the races but I would very much doubt it without help from the U.S.," he said.
"We still have problems with EMU (European Economic and Monetary Union). We do have a lot of numbers this week so that will have an effect on gilts," he added.
Beauchamp said good support for the contract arrived this session at 113-27, the top of the previous range.
Analysts at the Royal Bank of Scotland put sturdy support at 111-24, which translates to about 50 percent of the pullback in the June contract of the April to May rally.

"The indicators are positioned in a fairly neutral state and are awaiting a price action breakout," they said in the Royal Bank of Scotland's weekly technical outlook. "Provided the 50 percent support at 111-24 continues to hold a buy dips strategy is recommended."
September gilts were quoted at 114-02, unchanged in early trade. September short sterling futures were also unchanged at 93.14.
Data on Monday includes April manufacturing output and industrial production, May producer prices and April housing starts.
